basic_identification.full_title: Automotive Vehicles — Noise Emitted by Moving Vehicles — Specification and Method of Measurement
basic_identification.sector_category: Transport Engineering / Automotive Braking Systems, Vehicle Testing, Steering and Performance Evaluation (approved by the Transport Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Automotive Braking Systems, Vehicle Testing and Performance Evaluation Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Automotive Braking Systems, Vehicle Testing and Performance Evaluation Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard specifies the requirements and test evaluation methods for determining the external noise emitted by road vehicles in moving condition (pass-by noise). It is structured in multiple parts based on vehicle classification: Part 1 specifies limits and measurement methods for L2 category two-wheelers; Part 2 specifies limits and methods for categories other than L2 and L5 (covering M and N passenger and commercial road vehicles); and Part 3 specifies limits and methods for L5 (three-wheelers), L7 (quadricycles), E-rickshaws, and E-carts. It establishes mandatory acoustic limits at the manufacturing stage to control environmental noise pollution.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under Rule 120 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR), 1989, all road-going vehicles manufactured or registered in India must undergo mandatory pass-by noise type-approval (homologation) testing. Compliance with IS 3028 noise limits must be certified by designated government testing agencies (such as ARAI, GARC, or ICAT) prior to commercial vehicle release. Non-conforming vehicles cannot be registered or legally operated on Indian public roads. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to acoustic emission parameters.

requirements.detail: Requires a standardized open-air testing pad comprising an acceleration track and a centralized measurement zone. Two microphones must be positioned symmetrically on both sides of the vehicle's driving centerline at a distance of 7.5 m ± 0.05 m from the path axis and at a height of 1.2 m ± 0.02 m above the track surface.

The test track pavement must satisfy strict ISO 10844 acoustic criteria. Pavement residual void content is limited to <= 8%, and the surface sound absorption coefficient must not exceed 0.10. Additionally, the macrotexture depth must be greater than or equal to 0.4 mm to prevent tire rolling-noise absorption or scattering.

Acoustic measurements are sensitive to atmospheric parameters. Outdoor wind speed at microphone height must not exceed 5 m/s during test intervals to prevent wind-induced microphone distortion. Background environmental ambient noise must be at least 10 dB(A) lower than the vehicle's peak emitted sound level.

The test evaluates sound levels under worst-case acceleration. The vehicle must approach the test line at a specified speed (or engine RPM) in a selected gear, and then accelerate at wide-open-throttle (WOT) until the rear of the vehicle exits the test zone. The peak sound level recorded on the sound level meter (A-weighted, fast response) is taken as the evaluation result.

Under Part 2 modern norms (aligned with ECE R51.03), maximum limits for passenger cars are set between 72 dB(A) to 75 dB(A), while heavy commercial vehicles (N3 category) are restricted based on engine power ranges (varying from 80 dB(A) to 85 dB(A) depending on engine output and GVW limits).

At least four measurements must be conducted on each side of the vehicle for each gear configuration. The test results are considered valid only if the difference between consecutive runs on the same side does not exceed 2 dB(A). The highest mean value calculated from the loudest side constitutes the official sound level.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 3028 is the mandatory national Indian Standard code of practice specifying specification and measurement methods for evaluating external noise emitted by moving road vehicles. Strictly enforced under the statutory Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR), all newly manufactured road vehicles (such as motorcycles, passenger cars, buses, commercial trucks, E-rickshaws, and three-wheelers) must undergo pass-by sound evaluation to obtain type-approval certification. It specifies an open-air acoustic testing layout where vehicles accelerate at wide-open-throttle over a specialized, low-absorption ISO 10844 pavement while microphones record sound levels from 7.5 meters away. It enforces strict decibel limits—such as 76 dB(A) for battery-operated E-rickshaws and small three-wheelers, 77 dB(A) for medium-sized motorcycles, and up to 85 dB(A) for massive commercial transport trucks—to minimize urban environmental noise pollution.
